key_insight: Online Experiential Learning (OEL) lets language models continuously improve by extracting and reusing knowledge from their real-world deployment interactions, turning lived experience into reusable training signal.
problem_solved: Traditional LM improvement relies on offline human annotations or simulated data and ignores the rich, actionable experience collected during deployment; OEL unlocks that untapped stream for ongoing model improvement and adaptation.
method: Extract transferable experiential knowledge from interaction trajectories (logs of prompts, model actions, user feedback) in an online fashion.
Accumulate and compress experiences into a persistent, queryable store (experience buffer or distilled corpus) that captures recurring patterns and corrective signals.

Use the accumulated experience to adapt the model online via lightweight updates (e.g., continual fine-tuning, experience-conditioned prompts, or retrieval-augmented generation) while preserving stability.
impact: Enables LMs to self-improve from deployment, reducing reliance on costly human annotation and simulated environments, and improving robustness, personalization, and long-term performance in real-world settings.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing two-stage flow: Interaction Trajectories → Experience Extraction → Experience Store → Online Model Adaptation

Timeline or streaming graphic showing continuous updates and stability mechanisms (e.g., checkpointing or replay)
paper_title: Online Experiential Learning for Language Models
paper_authors: Tianzhu Ye, Li Dong, Qingxiu Dong, Xun Wu, Shaohan Huang
